content:
If a supplier's plan comes to fruition, some memory chips used in Apple devices will be manufactured in the United States for the first time.

According to the latest report, Apple's memory supplier SK hynix is in discussions with Intel, looking to use Intel's planned chip fabrication plant in Ohio...

Reuters reports that although details remain unclear, this South Korean company produces RAM and flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Some processors used in Apple devices are already manufactured in the U.S., but due to restrictions on foreign companies using TSMC's most advanced processes, these processors can only be used in older models. However, since Apple uses industry-standard versions, DRAM or NAND flash memory chips are not subject to such restrictions.

However, the report also notes that the plan may face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea may share Taiwan's concerns about exporting chip manufacturing technology, even when it involves older process nodes.

SK hynix stated that no decisions have been made yet. Intel declined to comment on the report, but confirmed it will continue moving forward with development plans for its Ohio project.
